_comment: Developer questions for the search measurement (search.py). Written from the corpus sources, before any model's summaries were read. 'answer' lists the corpus files that answer the question (relative to the prepared corpus, as score.py names them); a hit is any of them. Most questions avoid the identifiers of the answer file on purpose: a question that names the class finds it by its name alone.

questions.q: Where are and/or/not condition trees evaluated against a file's size, line count and modification date?
Which code rejects a routing condition that sets more than one branch or has a date it cannot parse?
Why do the combinators wrap their child conditions in a separate list type instead of holding the list directly?
Where are exact, model-free regex match counts computed and put in front of the summary of an oversized file?
What can happen when a source file does not fit into the model's context window, and what is the default?
How is the setting for files that are too large for the context parsed, and which values does it accept?
Where are the maximum number of input characters and the characters-per-token estimate for trimming the input configured?
Which mutable settings object carries top-p, min-p, repeat penalty and the other sampling parameters from the build configuration to the providers?
Which object holds the run-wide settings such as base directory, output directory, subtrees, excludes and file-size limits?
Where is the switch defined that only plans a run without generating anything?
Where is a model's leading thinking block removed from the answer before it is stored?
What happens when the model runs out of tokens while it is still reasoning, before the thinking block is closed?
Which interface does a new AI backend have to implement, and how does it report generation timings?
How is the backend chosen by name between the mock, the local llama.cpp and the OpenAI-compatible one?
Can a single model definition use a different backend than the one the run names?
Where is the GGUF model loaded on first use, with GPU offload, flash attention and KV cache types applied?
Where does the local backend keep mixture-of-experts weights on the CPU so a larger model fits into VRAM?
Which immutable value object, built with a builder, holds the configuration the local llama.cpp backend runs with?
Where are a model's reasoning effort and reasoning token budget kept?
How is the chat-completions request for OpenRouter built, and when are the seed and stop strings sent?
Where is it prevented that an API key goes out in cleartext over plain HTTP to a host that is not local?
Where is a failed HTTP response turned into an exception message with a shortened response body?
Which table definition makes sure a book never has more free copies than copies in total?
Where is the partial index on loans that have not been returned yet?
Which view lists overdue loans with the number of days they are late?

How is the late fee for a returned book calculated, and is it capped?
What stops a blocked member from borrowing a book?
Where is every checkout and return written to an audit trail?
Which change introduces library branches and individual book copies with barcodes?
Where was the column with the date a member joined renamed?
How many members and loans does the test data of the lending library contain?
Where is stock reserved when an item is added to a web-shop order, and the order total kept current?
Which procedure merges a supplier feed into the warehouse stock levels and logs how many rows were inserted and updated?
What happens to the nightly stock synchronisation when it fails halfway?

Where is the single-producer, single-consumer byte queue implemented, including the wrap-around copy?
Why must the buffer capacity be a power of two, and how many bytes does the buffer actually hold?
Which error codes can initialising the byte ring buffer return?
Where is a byte histogram computed on the GPU, with per-work-group counts in local memory and a reduction pass?
Which script sums revenue per month and region from CSV order exports?
